title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Vegetation — 2024
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Describe the major vegetation zones of Nepal according to altitude.
questions.solution: **Tropical (<1000 m):** sal (*Shorea robusta*), simal. **Sub-tropical (1000–2000 m):** chir pine, alder. **Temperate (2000–3000 m):** oak, rhododendron. **Sub-alpine (3000–4000 m):** fir, birch, juniper. **Alpine (>4000 m):** meadows, cushion plants; **nival:** permanent snow, no vegetation.
questions.knowledgeNote: Nepal compresses tropics-to-tundra into 200 km — the world's steepest vegetation staircase.

questions.question: Distinguish between tropical deciduous and temperate evergreen forests of Nepal.
questions.solution:
**Tropical deciduous** (Terai–Siwalik, <1000 m): shed leaves in dry summer (sal, simal); hot monsoon climate.

**Temperate evergreen** (Mahabharat–mid-hills, 2000–3000 m): retain leaves year-round (oak, rhododendron, pines); cool with winter frost.
questions.knowledgeNote: Deciduousness dodges drought; evergreenness endures cold — leaf habit maps directly onto climate stress.

questions.question: In which vegetation zone is sal (*Shorea robusta*) dominant? Write two of its economic uses.
questions.solution:
**Tropical zone** (Terai and Siwalik, below ~1000 m) — sal forms nearly pure stands.

**Uses:** premier construction timber (houses, sleepers) and leaves as traditional plates (duna-tapari) plus religious offerings.
questions.knowledgeNote: Sal's resinous durability made it the Terai's timber backbone — and the centre of community-forestry conflicts.

questions.question: What are the major causes of deforestation in Nepal?
questions.solution: Fuel-wood dependence, agricultural expansion and resettlement, illegal logging and smuggling, infrastructure (roads, dams), forest fires, and overgrazing.
questions.knowledgeNote: Community forestry reversed the 1980s crisis in the hills — the Terai frontier remains the pressure point.

questions.question: What is community forestry? Explain its role in vegetation conservation in Nepal.
questions.solution:
**Community forestry** hands state forests to local user groups who protect, harvest sustainably, and share benefits.

It reversed hill deforestation: user groups patrol, replant, and regulate grazing — forest cover in programme areas has measurably regenerated while funding schools and trails.
questions.knowledgeNote: Nepal's programme is a global model — devolution succeeding where central policing failed.

questions.question: Distinguish between in-situ and ex-situ conservation with one Nepalese example of each.
questions.solution:
**In-situ:** protecting species in natural habitat — e.g. Chitwan National Park (rhino, tiger).

**Ex-situ:** protecting outside habitat — e.g. Central Zoo, Lalitpur, or the Godavari botanical garden seed banks.

In-situ preserves evolution in place; ex-situ is the backup for the critically endangered.
questions.knowledgeNote: 12 national parks + reserves + conservation areas form Nepal's in-situ network — pair the concept with the map.
